title: cross-region-rbac-simulator-kms-staging-and-audit-ledger
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Add a cross-region RBAC v2 simulator, a KMS staging (dry-run) mode, and append-only audit ledger hashing to help compliance teams validate policy changes and key routing before enforceable rollouts. Motivation: recent incidents and compliance reviews highlighted that policy interactions across tenant, zone, and KMS routing are hard to reason about without a repeatable simulation harness. This change lets SRE/security/product run 'what-if' scenarios and get deterministic diffs for audit review.

What this PR contains (single-line sections): Implementation: 1) rbac/simulator: an offline policy evaluator that ingests current RBAC v2 policies, tenant attributes, and geo/zone constraints and produces access decisions and resource-affinity maps; supports batch scenarios and single-request traces with KV-cache-aware path simulation. 2) kms/staging: KMS client shim that supports 'staging' mode where routing decisions are recorded and returned as dry-run metadata (no CMK use) and integrates with the simulator so teams can validate that key affinity/residency rules will pick the expected provider. 3) audit/ledger: append-only ledger writer that emits canonicalized entries plus a running SHA256-based cumulative hash (audit chain) for each tenant-zone pairing; ledger entries include simulator diffs and KMS staging outcomes when run together. 4) rollout: feature-flagged shadow rollout wiring (config flag: security.simulator.shadow_rollout) and a migration tool to export simulation reports for the Compliance workspace.

Key design notes: - Simulator is intentionally conservative: deny precedence mirrors production evaluator, but simulator emits a 'confidence' score when policy precedence is ambiguous. - KMS staging does not touch key material and is safe to enable in production for read-only simulation; explicit opt-in required per tenant. - Audit ledger format is stable JSON Lines with canonical ordering; the cumulative hash allows downstream auditors to verify ledger integrity.

Behavioral changes / compatibility: No breaking API changes. Feature gated: all functionality off by default. Customers will not see enforced policy changes until rollouts are promoted.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for policy rules, property tests for comparator invariants, integration harness that runs full-stack simulations against a small test cluster, and e2e smoke tests that verify audit ledger hashes are stable across restarts. A compliance export job was added to produce zipped reports with simulator diffs and signatures.

Rollback plan: Disable the shadow_rollout flag and remove staging permissions; auditors can still validate prior simulation reports. If ledger load causes issues, we fall back to the legacy audit writer (feature flag: audit.legacy_writer_enabled).

Related work: complements ENG-6482 (policy-decision-cache) and ENG-7305 (kms-affinity-refactor). Linear tasks: ENG-7521, ENG-7598. Support ticket SUP-3410 requested a compliance staging path.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests for simulator - [x] Docs (security runbook) drafted - [x] Compliance export job implemented - [x] Feature flags in place

review_comments: Noah Patel: Can the simulator emit a compact policy-diff artifact suitable for automated regression detection? Asked to add a JSON delta summary. (resolved)
Riley Chen: Suggest making the ledger hashing pluggable so FIPS customers can choose alternate hash algorithms. Request recorded; added pluggable interface. (resolved)
Samir Kapoor: Concerned about perf impact when running large batch scenarios; requested throttling controls and streaming outputs for reports. We added an async streaming report mode. (resolved)
QA Lead (Tara O'Neal): Found flaky test in trace_test.go on CI; root cause fixed by adding deterministic RNG seeding. (resolved)
release_notes: Added a cross-region RBAC v2 simulator, a KMS staging (dry-run) mode for validating key routing, and an append-only audit ledger with cumulative hashing. Feature gated and off by default; provides compliance teams with deterministic simulation reports and exportable artifacts.
